thread:
Alex: heads-up — running into inconsistent abort semantics between Node and Python SDKs for streaming responses. Node stops streaming immediately on AbortController.abort(), Python sometimes finishes the final chunk and leaves the connection open for a short while. Anyone seen this? :thinking:
Mira: I have. Usually comes down to how the SDK wraps the transport + whether the client calls close() vs just signals cancellation. Also server treats mid-stream cancel differently (499 vs 200).
CJ: fwiw we saw duplicate tokens when retry logic kicks in after an abort. If the client retries non-idempotent streaming requests we get repeated output.
Sam: can you paste minimal repro for both? small snippets are perfect. :ear:
Alex: sure — Node snippet:
```javascript
const ac = new AbortController();
fetch('/v1/stream', { signal: ac.signal })
// ...later
ac.abort();
```
Python snippet:
```python
with client.stream("/v1/stream") as s:
    # some condition
    s.cancel()  # this triggers SDK-level cancel
```
Mira: that matches what I've debugged. Node's fetch signals the kernel and we get a socket FIN quickly. Python's streaming wrapper often drains the generator or waits for server EOF before bubbling up CancelledError. Transport implementation differences (httpx vs node-fetch) matter.
CJ: reminder: our retry middleware currently treats Abort errors as transient in some SDKs. We should document: aborts from user should NOT trigger automatic retries for non-idempotent streaming/generation calls.
deploy-bot: runtime-metrics: observed ~120 cancels yesterday; 73% from node-sdk, 21% python-sdk, remainder mobile. Logs show 499 at edge for node cancels; python cancels show 200 + connection closed by client after few ms.
Mira: proposal: define interop conformance: 1) user abort -> SDK surfaces AbortError/CancelledError immediately, 2) SDK should close underlying connection, 3) server should surface 499-ish so logs reflect client cancel, 4) no automatic retries for aborted non-idempotent calls.
Alex: agreed. Also need to ensure streaming state machines don't race on teardown (e.g., buffer flush + cancel).
Sam: action: I'll add a failing test in sdk-conformance that simulates mid-stream abort and asserts no retry + client error. ETA EOD today.
Mira: I'll take Python SDK fix — ensure our stream wrapper calls `transport.aclose()` immediately and raises CancelledError.
Alex: I'll own Node change — ensure AbortController is proxied to underlying fetch/socket and that our retry hooks treat it as terminal for this request. I'll open PR with test.
CJ: I'll update the spec doc (RFC) and add the expected server status codes and logging conventions.
Sam: ping me @Sam when PRs are up, I'll run infra conformance and attach CI traces. :+1:
Alex: thanks all. I'll drop the Node repro and failing test in #sdk-conformance and tag you both. Keeping this thread for any follow-ups.
Mira: tiny note — mobile SDK (iOS) uses URLSession tasks cancel semantics; might need a small adapter. Will file follow-up ticket.
CJ: adding ticket now: STACK-412 abort-interop-stream-teardown.
Alex: closing loop: expected timeline — tests + PRs in next 48h, spec update before EOW.
Sam: sounds good.
